meta.audience: The twelve and the multitude, in turn
meta.location: The temple in the land Bountiful
meta.unit: The sacrament and the departure (3 Nephi 18)
principles: A rule about who may be turned away and who may not
A departure witnessed by the disciples

world_behind.title: The words of the ordinance are kept in another book
world_behind.text: This chapter gives the acts and not the prayers. Moroni 4:3 and Moroni 5:2 preserve the exact forms, and Moroni 4:1 says they were administered according to the commandments of Christ, which is a claim about this occasion.

world_behind.title: The second administration has no supply at all
world_behind.text: Verses 1 and 2 send disciples away to fetch bread and wine. 3 Nephi 20:6 and 7 report that no bread and no wine had been brought by anyone, and that he gave both to them regardless. The two meals of the visit are told with opposite logistics.

world_behind.title: The ordination named here has its form in Moroni 3
world_behind.text: Verse 5 says one shall be ordained with power to administer the bread. Moroni 3:3 preserves the sentence used, which names the authority, the office, and the work in one line.

world_behind.title: The audience shifts follow the pattern of the whole day
world_behind.text: Verse 5 addresses the disciples, verse 17 the multitude, verse 26 the disciples again. 3 Nephi 13:25, 15:11 and 17:1 make the same turns earlier, so instructions for the leadership are kept separable from instructions for everyone.

world_behind.title: The disputations are older than this chapter
world_behind.text: Verse 34 gives these commandments because of the disputations among them, and 3 Nephi 11:28 had already forbidden disputations about baptism at the start of the same day. The visit opens and closes by naming the same fault.

world_behind.title: Mormon steps out of the quotation once
world_behind.text: Verse 37 breaks off to promise the reader that what is written about the giving of the Holy Ghost is true, and 3 Nephi 19:13 delivers it. The abridger is the only voice in the chapter that speaks to somebody outside the scene.

world_behind.title: The cloud is the detail Acts keeps too
world_behind.text: Verse 38 says a cloud overshadowed the multitude so that they saw him not, and Acts 1:9 has a cloud receive him out of the apostles' sight. Two accounts of an ascension a hemisphere apart record the same obstruction.

words.text: A loaf, and food in general. The record uses the word twenty-two times and the King James Bible three hundred and sixty-one. Verse 1 has it sent for rather than already present.
The fermented drink of the vine. It appears forty times in the record, and the King James Bible two hundred and thirty-one. Alma 55 uses the same word for the drink that put a guard to sleep.
Keep, carry out, do as prescribed. The record uses the word twenty-six times and the King James Bible fifty-five. Verse 6 sets the pattern by what he has just done.
Calling to mind, and a memorial. The word turns up twenty-eight times here, and the King James Bible fifty-one. Verses 7 and 11 give the body and the blood as its objects.
Bedrock, a foundation that will not shift. The record uses the word thirty-four times and the King James Bible one hundred and nineteen. Verses 12 and 13 hold it against a sandy foundation.

In a manner not fitting the thing being done. Its count is four times in this book, while the King James Bible twice, both in 1 Corinthians 11. Verse 28 makes it the disciples' responsibility to prevent.
To serve, and to administer an ordinance. Thirty-five uses here against one hundred in the King James Bible. Verses 30 and 32 use it of a man who has been refused the emblems.

phrases.term: He took of the bread and brake and blessed it
phrases.text: The order of actions, given as narrative before it becomes a rule. Verse 6 turns the sequence into the instruction.

phrases.term: This shall ye always observe to do, even as I have done
phrases.text: The pattern is his own act. Verse 6 defines the ordinance by pointing back a few sentences.

phrases.term: It shall be a testimony unto the Father that ye do always remember me
phrases.text: The ordinance is addressed to the Father. Moroni 4:3 will put that same sentence into the prayer itself.

phrases.term: If ye do always remember me ye shall have my Spirit to be with you
phrases.text: The promise attached to the bread, repeated word for word at verse 11 for the wine.

phrases.term: Whoso among you shall do more or less than these
phrases.text: A boundary in both directions. Adding to the ordinance and subtracting from it get the same verdict.

phrases.term: Ye must watch and pray always, lest ye be tempted by the devil
phrases.text: Given first to the disciples in verse 15 and then to the multitude in verse 18, with the wording adjusted for each.

phrases.term: Pray in your families unto the Father, always in my name
phrases.text: Household prayer commanded directly, with wives and children named as the ones to be blessed.

phrases.term: Ye shall not forbid any man from coming unto you when ye shall meet together
phrases.text: The meeting is open. Verse 23 adds that those who come are to be prayed for.

phrases.term: Hold up your light that it may shine unto the world
phrases.text: The light is identified in the same verse: it is what they have seen him do.

phrases.term: Ye shall not cast him out of your synagogues, or your places of worship
phrases.text: The refusal at verse 29 is limited here. A man kept from the emblems still keeps his seat.

phrases.term: He touched with his hand the disciples whom he had chosen, one by one
phrases.text: The same method used with the children in 3 Nephi 17:21. Verse 37 says the multitude did not hear what he said as he touched them.

verses.label: v. 1–2
verses.title: An errand and an interval both recorded
verses.text: The record notes what happened while nothing was happening: "while they were gone for bread and wine, he commanded the multitude that they should sit themselves down upon the earth." The bread and wine are not produced miraculously here, as they are one chapter later at 3 Nephi 20:6–7 where the record explicitly denies any were brought. Two accounts of the same ordinance stand two chapters apart, one with a supply run and one with none, and the record marks the difference by reporting the errand.

verses.label: v. 3–9
verses.title: A meal that satisfies, stated four times
verses.text: The record uses the same word of both elements and of both groups: the disciples "had eaten and were filled," the multitude "had eaten and were filled," the disciples "did drink of it and were filled," and the multitude "did drink, and they were filled." Four uses in seven verses. The Gospel accounts at Matthew 26:26–28 and Luke 22:19–20 report the distribution without any statement about sufficiency. Here the record makes fullness part of what is being described.

verses.label: v. 36–37
verses.title: Testimony sorted by who could hear
verses.text: The record reports that part of the event went unwitnessed: "the multitude heard not the words which he spake, therefore they did not bear record; but the disciples bare record that he gave them power to give the Holy Ghost." Two groups are present, one can testify and one cannot, and the reason is acoustic rather than spiritual. The compiler then adds a promise in his own voice, "I will show unto you hereafter that this record is true," which puts a forward reference into the middle of a narrative and makes the claim checkable against what follows.

chapter.title: The ordinance is taught by being done
chapter.text: Verse 3 is the act and verse 6 is the rule. The pattern is fixed by pointing at something that just happened in the room.

chapter.title: Everyone is filled
chapter.text: Verses 4 and 9 say the multitude ate and drank until filled. The scene is a meal before it is a symbol.

chapter.title: The promise is stated twice in identical words
chapter.text: Verses 7 and 11 attach the Spirit to always remembering him. The repetition marks the bread and the wine as one instruction.

chapter.title: Both directions of change are ruled out
chapter.text: Verse 13 names doing more and doing less together. The form is treated as fixed.

chapter.title: The same charge is fitted to two audiences
chapter.text: Verse 15 gives the disciples the devil and verse 18 gives the multitude the sifting. The counsel is adjusted to who is hearing it.

chapter.title: Two kinds of exclusion are separated
chapter.text: Verse 29 keeps an unworthy man from the emblems and verse 32 keeps him in the building. The chapter is careful about which door closes.

chapter.title: The reason for the rules is stated at the end
chapter.text: Verse 34 names the disputations. The chapter explains itself after giving the instruction.

chapter.title: The departure is quiet
chapter.text: Verse 38 puts a cloud between him and the multitude, and verse 39 gives the ascension to the disciples alone. The day ends with most of the crowd unable to see.

applications.title: Show the thing before you explain it
applications.text: He broke the bread, blessed it, gave it, and only then said what it meant and told them to keep doing it. Demonstration first and instruction second is the order here, and it is the harder way round to organise.

applications.title: Say the whole promise for each half
applications.text: The clause "if ye do always remember me ye shall have my Spirit to be with you" is given after the bread and again, word for word, after the wine. Repeating a promise in full rather than referring back to it is what makes it available to somebody who joined late.

applications.title: Keep the form as it was given
applications.text: Doing more and doing less are named as the same failure. When you have been handed a practice, the impulse to improve it deserves the same scrutiny as the impulse to skip it.

applications.title: Give the reason that fits the hearer
applications.text: The same instruction to watch and pray is put to the disciples and to the multitude with different warnings attached. When you pass on a discipline, attach the reason that fits the person in front of you rather than the one that fits you.

applications.title: Pray where your family can hear
applications.text: He commanded household prayer specifically, "that your wives and your children may be blessed." Praying alone is not the whole of it; some of it has to happen where the people you live with are standing.

applications.title: Do not forbid, and keep praying for them
applications.text: The rule about meetings is stated twice inside one verse, "ye shall not forbid any man from coming unto you... and forbid them not," and the follow-up is an instruction to pray for the person. Exclusion is refused and responsibility is added.

applications.title: Hold up the light you have actually seen
applications.text: The instruction names its own content: "I am the light which ye shall hold up—that which ye have seen me do." What you offer other people should be a thing you watched happen rather than a thing you were told about.

applications.title: Keep the door open to the person you had to refuse
applications.text: He allows withholding the ordinance and then forbids casting the person out, twice, and adds that you may be the means of bringing them back. A boundary and an ongoing welcome are made compatible in three verses.

questions.text: What would always remembering him change about this week?
Do I take the emblems as a witness, or as a habit?
Where have I added to or trimmed something I was given whole?
What am I not watching for?
When did my family last hear me pray?
Who have I quietly hoped would stop coming?
Which of my disputations would this chapter have been given for?
